name: space-cycle-edit-focus-gate
description: Live check: Cmd+Shift+Right/Left are now SHIPPED DEFAULTS for nextSpace/previousSpace (the direct user report), and both are also AppKit's standard extend-selection-to-line-end chord, so the edit-focus gate must cover them - this is the first shipped default in the gated set. Extends the edit-focus-gate.json mechanism (same fixture page reporting its input selection into document.title via TabEventForwarder::TitleWasSet, same gate vlog lines) rather than inventing a new one; the only new ingredient is a THREE-space fixture (space-cycle.spaces.json) so a cold, never-yet-visited space's tab materializing on landing gives an objective, per-hop-unique vlog line for 'the space really switched', not just 'the gate said fire'. Starts on the MIDDLE space (Elsewhere) so both neighbors are cold: phase 0 proves nextSpace's Cmd+Shift+Right switches forward (Elsewhere -> Third, Third's tab materializes for the first time); phase 1 proves previousSpace's Cmd+Shift+Left switches backward twice (Third -> Elsewhere -> Editing, Editing's tab materializing for the first time, landing on the gate test's own field); phase 2 is the positive-control/gated-block pair, run for Cmd+Shift+Right specifically (the exact combo named in the bug report) against that now-focused field.

actions.note: let the sidebar render and the startup space's (Elsewhere) tab commit
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot; without this every key/click lands in Finder

PHASE 0, THE CHECK (nextSpace default): nothing editable focused, so the gate short-circuits to fire on kind=none - this is the SHIPPED DEFAULT, no hotkeys.json override at all. Should land on Third, whose tab has never been active and is therefore cold (the landing semantics).

OBJECTIVE PROOF nextSpace really switched (not just that the gate decided fire in the abstract): Third's tab was cold at launch, so this URL can only commit if the space actually changed and materialized it.
PHASE 1a: previousSpace default, first hop, Third -> Elsewhere. Elsewhere was the startup space so its tab is already live - this hop is just transit, nothing new to assert.

PHASE 1b, THE CHECK (previousSpace default): second hop, Elsewhere -> Editing. Editing's tab has never been active either, so it is still cold - a second independent materialize proof, and it also lands us on the gate test's own field-bearing page.
OBJECTIVE PROOF previousSpace really switched, same reasoning as the nextSpace check above, using the one other tab that was cold at launch.
C++ pushed a positive kNone for the freshly-committed page, same pre-condition edit-focus-gate.json checks before clicking in
PHASE 2 SETUP: click into the field (measured centre, per edit-focus-gate.json). Its focus handler puts the caret at the END of "hello world" and reports the collapsed range.
kPageEditable pushed - the gate's real signal has arrived

Re-click the SAME already-focused field near its left inner edge to move the caret near the START of "hello world" without a blur/refocus cycle (the page's 'focus' listener - which resets the caret to the end - only fires on the blurred-to-focused transition, not on a second click while already focused). This is what makes Cmd+Shift+RIGHT's extend-to-end meaningful: extending right from the end would be a no-op. MEASURED, not guessed: pixel-scanned edit-focus-gate.json's own phase1-blocked capture - the field's rendered border starts at x=259, inner white at x=263, first glyph stroke of 'hello' at x=271. The old x=250 sat 9-13px LEFT of that border, on page background, which is what blurred the field before the chord arrived. x=280 lands ~17px inside the measured inner edge, safely inside the input and still left of the text midpoint (~x=327), so the selection this produces still meaningfully differs from the end.

PHASE 2, THE CHECK (the exact combo from the bug report): gated chord with a page text field focused. Must NOT switch space and must NOT open anything - must extend the field's selection to the end of the line instead.
still the Editing space, still the fixture page, no space-switch chrome change, "hello world" partially selected from the click point to the end

PHASE 3 SETUP (the control): click a neutral part of the page - empty background - to blur the input, same coordinates edit-focus-gate.json uses. Both phases click into this same window first, so the only difference is WHERE it lands.
blur observed - back to kNone, nothing typable holds the keyboard

PHASE 3, THE CONTROL: the very same gated chord, same shipped default, now that nothing editable has focus. Must FIRE and switch space - proof phase 2's block came from live focus state, not from the hotkey being dead. Elsewhere is already materialized (the startup space) so no fresh commit is expected; ax_window_count below is the corroboration instead.
back on Elsewhere - the same chord that was blocked moments ago now fires

assertions.label: next-space-default-switched
assertions.desc: Cmd+Shift+Right, the shipped default with no rebind, switched to a space whose tab had never been active - only possible if nextSpace actually fired and the space actually changed.

assertions.label: previous-space-default-switched
assertions.desc: Cmd+Shift+Left, the shipped default with no rebind, switched to the OTHER space whose tab had never been active.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: edit focus gate fire \(native route\)
assertions.label: native-route-owns-the-chord
assertions.desc: Cmd+Shift+Arrow is now matched in prePerformKeyEquivalent (NativeHotkeyAction::kNextSpace) instead of by a SwiftUI keyboardShortcut, because the HTML sidebar's WebContents swallowed the chord before SwiftUI ever saw it. This line only appears when the native map MATCHED the event - MatchAction runs first and returns to super without gating when nothing matches - so it is the proof the new route, not the old one, is carrying the switch.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: edit focus gate pass-page-editable \(native route\)
assertions.label: native-route-yields-to-a-focused-field
assertions.desc: + the native route must keep yielding Cmd+Shift+Right to a focused text field (ComboEditsText classifies cmd+shift+arrow as text-editing). Unlike the swift-route line below, this one is NOT deduped to decision transitions - MayFireHotkeyForEvent logs every gated press - so it records the actual keystroke rather than a render.

assertions.label: keystroke-reached-the-field
assertions.desc: Effect: the fixture page's own selection report crossed the bridge into the run log. -11 is the line's end, so Cmd+Shift+Right performed its real AppKit moveToRightEndOfLineAndModifySelection: job INSIDE the field - this also independently proves the space did not switch, since a switch would have blurred the field and reported ATRIUM-SEL-blurred instead.

Exactly one window throughout: unlike edit-focus-gate.json (which rebinds the chord onto the native openCommandBar intercept too, so its control opens a second window), this task's defaults never open a palette - the corroboration here is that the control's space-switch is a same-window navigation, not a new surface.
